title: The Songs of Ascents
lead: Fifteen short psalms (120–134) carry the title "A song of the ascents." They were probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts, and the Mishnah links their number to the fifteen steps of the temple. Christians call them the Gradual Psalms.

sections.b: Israel's law called every man to "appear before the LORD" three times a year at the feasts (Exodus 23:14–17; Deuteronomy 16:16), and the Bible always speaks of "going up" to Jerusalem, which stands high in the Judean hills (1 Samuel 1:3; Psalm 122:4; Luke 2:41–42). Isaiah pictures pilgrims singing on the way "to the mountain of the LORD" (Isaiah 30:29, fresh rendering), and Jeremiah's watchmen call, "Get up, let us go up to Zion" (Jeremiah 31:6, fresh rendering). The Hebrew word for these songs, ma'alot, "ascents," comes from the same verb 'alah, "go up." Ezra calls the return from Babylon "the journey up" (Ezra 7:9), and Jesus' last journey to Jerusalem is told as a going up (Mark 10:32–33).
